verdict.rationale: Snowflake documents streams that record DML changes on tables "so that actions can be taken using the changed data" (change capture for incremental processing). It also has dynamic tables (GA in release notes) and dbt Projects on Snowflake, which develops, deploys and orchestrates transformations inside the platform; Snowpipe adds continuous micro-batch ingestion. Missing for 10: any evidence of Tasks for scheduled or triggered execution, documentation of how dynamic tables refresh declaratively or incrementally (only a release-note title), and independent hands-on corroboration of continuous transformation pipelines.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I can run continuous or incremental transformations — streams, tasks, declarative pipelines, or continuous queries — inside the platform

citations.quote: A stream object records data manipulation language (DML) changes made to tables, including inserts (including COPY INTO), updates, and deletes, as well as metadata about each change, so that actions can be taken using the changed data.
CREATE OR ALTER DYNAMIC TABLE (General availability)
dbt Projects on Snowflake brings the full dbt lifecycle into Snowflake: develop, deploy, orchestrate, and observe your transformations in the same place your data already lives.
Snowpipe continuously loads data from files into standard tables and Apache Iceberg™ tables as the files arrive in a stage.
